protocol.item: GENERAL MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLES OF A POISONED/OVERDOSE PATIENT
protocol.source_text:
GENERAL MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLES OF A POISONED/OVERDOSE PATIENT 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Resuscitation 
•
Airway 
•
Breathing 
•
Circulation 
•
Seizure control 
•
Correct hypoglycaemia 
•
Correct hyperthermia 
•
Resuscitation antidotes 
e.g. atropine for organophosphates;  NaHCO3 for tricyclic antidepressants & 
salicylates, HIET for b-blockers  
 
Risk Assessment 
•
Agent(s) 
•
Dose(s) 
•
Time since ingestion 
•
Current clinical status 
•
Patient factors 
 
Supportive Care & Monitoring 
•
FASTHUGS IN BED Please (see box) – applies where appropriate 
 
Investigations 
•
ECG and paracetamol level for ALL 
•
Further tests are required as indicated by the specific presentation 
•
Rationale for investigations 
•
Refine risk assessment or prognosis 
•
Exclude or confirm an important differential 
•
Exclude or confirm an important specific poisoning 
•
Exclude or confirm a complication requiring specific management 
•
Establish an indication for antidote administration 
•
Establish an indication for institution of enhanced elimination 
•
Monitor response to therapy 
•
Define an endpoint for therapeutic interventions 
Remembered by the mnemonic “Resus – RSI – DEAD” 
 
Decontamination & Enhanced Elimination 
•
Activated charcoal (1g/kg) may be considered if a patient has 
ingested a potentially life-threatening quantity of substance/s and 
presents within 1 hour of ingestion 
•
Consider transferring for dialysis (see box) 
 
Antidotes 
 
Antidote 
Substance  
Atropine 
Organophosphate & carbamates 
Calcium gluconate/chloride, HIET 
Calcium channel blockers 
Desferrioximine 
Iron 
Ethanol, Folic acid 
Methanol 
HIET (high-dose insulin euglycaemic therapy) 
b blockers 
Intralipd 
Local anaesthetic 
Methylene blue 
Methaemaglobinaemia 
N-acetylcysteine 
Paracetamol 
Pyridoxine 
Isoniazid 
Sodium bicarbonate 
Tricyclic antidepressants; salicylates 
Vit K; FFPs 
Warfarin 
 
Disposition 
•
Urgent GIT referral  
FASTHUGS IN BED Please 
F – fluid therapy & feeding 
A – analgesia & antiemetics 
S – sedation 
T – thrombo-prophylaxis 
H – head up position (30°)  
U – ulcer prophylaxis 
G – glucose control 
S – skin/eye care; suctioning 
I – indwelling catheter 
N – nasogastric tube 
B – bowel cares 
E – environment (temp control) 
D – de-escalation 
P – psychosocial support 
Ingestions that may require dialysis 
Barbiturates 
Salicylates 
Lithium 
Toxic alcohols i.e. methanol, ethanol, ethylene glycol 
Theophylline/Caffeine 
INH 
Metformin 
Dabigatran 
Sodium valproate 
Carbamazepine
